Authors: Chu, J.; He, M.; Kontogeorgis, G. M.; Liu, X.; Liang, X.
Title: Screening HFC/HFO and ionic liquid for absorption refrigeration at the atomic scale by the prediction model of machine learning
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Employs Attention-Enhanced GNN (AEGNN) with disconnected cation/anion/refrigerant graphs and ambient T/P for HFC/HFO solubility prediction, demonstrating high R2 on random splits.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Primary direct baseline and benchmark reference in Intro §1 & Discussion §4
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Chu et al. evaluate exclusively under random splitting without testing OOD generalization. Our work establishes a 5-tier Generalization Ladder, reveals corresponding-states thermodynamic grounding, epistemic uncertainty guardrails, and stereochemical representation limits.

Authors: Qin, H.; Wang, Z.; Ruan, J.; et al.
Title: Integrating machine learning model and computer-aided molecular design toward rational ionic liquid selection for separating fluorinated refrigerants
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Combines ANN-group contribution models with computer-aided ionic liquid design (CAILD) to screen entrainers for separating fluorinated refrigerant azeotropes (e.g., R410A).
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Industrial separation application anchor in Intro §1.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Focuses on downstream separation process optimization using group-contribution ML; does not investigate graph representation bottlenecks, OOD generalization bounds, or corresponding-states feature regularization.

Title: Thermodynamic consistency and neural network modeling of gas solubility in ionic liquids
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Applies Gibbs-Duhem and equation-of-state thermodynamic consistency tests to evaluate the quality of experimental gas–IL solubility data used for training neural networks.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Data quality and thermodynamic consistency anchor in Methods §2.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Employs conventional shallow ANNs for individual gas systems; does not formulate multi-component molecular graph architectures, generalizability ladders, or multi-species transfer.

Title: Structure-based out-of-distribution materials property prediction: a benchmark study
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Systematically demonstrates that random splitting yields inflated performance metrics in materials ML due to compositional redundancy, calling for rigorous OOD benchmarks.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Core methodological justification for OOD benchmark design in Intro §1.2 & Methods §2.4
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Focuses on inorganic crystalline materials; our work provides the counterpart for multi-component fluid phase equilibrium thermodynamics and ionic liquid solutions.

Title: Machine learning-guided discovery of ionic polymer electrolytes for lithium metal batteries
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Combines quantum chemistry and GCNNs for ionic materials, explicitly documenting that multiple temperature data points per IL cause random splits to yield deceptively high accuracy.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Core anchor for multi-condition data leakage in Methods §2.1 & Discussion §4.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Addresses solid polymer electrolytes for batteries; our work addresses vapor–liquid phase equilibrium of fluorinated gases in ionic liquids across chemical families.

Authors: Wu, Z.; Ramsundar, B.; Feinberg, E. N.; et al.
Title: MoleculeNet: A benchmark for molecular machine learning
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Establishes standard molecular ML benchmarks and formalizes scaffold splitting to simulate out-of-distribution medicinal chemistry deployment.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Foundational reference for non-random splitting protocols in Methods §2.4
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Scaffold splitting is designed for single drug-like molecules; we formalize the multi-component chemical generalization ladder for ternary solvent–solute mixtures.

Title: Geometry-complete perceptual neural network for 3D molecular and macromolecular representations
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Develops an SE(3)-equivariant, chirality-aware geometry-complete perceptual GNN that formally resolves stereochemical equivalence in molecular representations.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Theoretical anchor for stereochemical representation limits in Methods §2.7 & Discussion §4.3
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We cite GCPNet to establish that 2D topological graphs and 3D stereochemical representations are fundamentally non-equivalent; we show that in the absence of training data support, adding stereo tags fails to generalize.

Title: Equivariant neural networks for complete molecular geometry and chirality
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Demonstrates the necessity of 3D geometric completeness and chiral invariants for differentiating enantiomers and diastereomers in deep learning.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Representation boundary reference in Discussion §4.3
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Highlights the theoretical necessity of 3D coordinates, supporting our finding that 2D topology exhibits a hard mathematical ceiling on R1336mzz(E/Z).

Title: Geometric message passing and chemical space generalization for molecular property prediction
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Analyzes the trade-offs between 2D topological graph scaling and 3D conformer generation across out-of-distribution chemical spaces.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Literature context for 2D vs 3D graph representations in Methods §2.2
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Confirms conformer generation uncertainty in fluid mixtures; supports our decision to use 2D tri-graphs regularized by thermodynamic invariants rather than speculative 3D solvation conformers.

Title: The Volumetric and Thermodynamic Properties of Fluids. I. Theoretical Basis and Virial Coefficients
Journal_or_Venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Formulates the three-parameter corresponding-states principle using the acentric factor (omega) to describe molecular shape and acentricity in fluid phase behavior.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Foundational thermodynamic theory for Mreduced in Methods §2.3 & Discussion §4.2
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Provides the physical derivation for using (Tr, Pr, omega) as universal thermodynamic scaling coordinates rather than raw unscaled (T, P).

Authors: Prausnitz, J. M.; Lichtenthaler, R. N.; de Azevedo, E. G.
Title: Molecular Thermodynamics of Fluid-Phase Equilibria (3rd Edition)
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Classic treatise establishing corresponding-states theory, intermolecular potential scaling, and liquid-phase activity coefficient foundations.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Standard textbook foundation for corresponding states in Methods §2.3
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Used to justify that fluids at identical reduced conditions (Tr, Pr) occupy corresponding states of intermolecular interaction.

Title: Thermodynamically consistent neural network models for phase equilibrium and equations of state
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Demonstrates that introducing dimensionless reduced coordinates and thermodynamic constraints into neural networks improves physical consistency.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Conceptual foundation for thermodynamic coordinate conditioning in Methods §2.3
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Focuses on bulk fluid equations of state; our work integrates corresponding states into multi-head graph attention networks for ternary ionic liquid mixtures.

Authors: Fredenslund, A.; Jones, R. L.; Prausnitz, J. M.
Title: Group-contribution estimation of activity coefficients in nonideal liquid mixtures
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Establishes the UNIFAC group contribution framework for predicting vapor–liquid equilibria from structural functional groups.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Classical baseline background in Intro §1.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We note that while UNIFAC is widely used, standard UNIFAC tables lack group interaction parameters for specialized fluorinated moieties in ionic liquids.

Authors: Lei, Z.; Dai, C.; Chen, B.
Title: Gas solubility in ionic liquids: UNIFAC model extension and molecular dynamics simulation
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Extends UNIFAC to ionic liquids, documenting the need for extensive experimental fitting for each newly synthesized IL anion/cation group.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Evidence for parameter scarcity in group-contribution models in Intro §1.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Confirms that group-contribution methods struggle when novel fluorinated refrigerants or newly designed fluorosulfonate anions are introduced without prior experimental parameters.

Title: COSMO-RS: a novel and efficient tool for the modern practical developer of liquid technology
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Introduces the Conductor-like Screening Model for Real Solvents (COSMO-RS), predicting chemical potentials from quantum-chemical screening charge surfaces.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Quantum-thermodynamic baseline in Intro §1.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We explain that COSMO-RS requires expensive DFT calculations for each ion conformer and exhibits known quantitative offsets for complex fluorinated dispersion forces.

Authors: Tropsha, A.; Gramatica, P.; Gombar, V. K.
Title: The importance of being earnest: validation of (Q)SAR models and applicability domain definition
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Formalizes the concept of applicability domains (AD) and distance-based thresholds in molecular property prediction.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Theoretical baseline for distance metrics in Intro §1.2 & Discussion §4.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We cite Tropsha to contextualize the classical AD hypothesis, and demonstrate that in multicomponent gas–IL absorption, no single scalar distance captures all shift dimensions.

Title: Current status of methods for defining the applicability domain of (quantitative) structure-activity relationships
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Comprehensive review of chemical distance metrics (Tanimoto, Euclidean, leverage) used to define applicability domains.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Methodological framing for D_FP and D_phys in Methods §2.4 & Discussion §4.1
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Supports our nuanced framing: existing distance-based AD strategies provide useful similarity diagnostics, but discrete structural transitions break monotonic error scaling.

Authors: Lakshminarayanan, B.; Pritzel, A.; Blundell, C.
Title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
Journal_or_Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Demonstrates that ensembles of randomly initialized neural networks provide high-quality, calibrated epistemic uncertainty estimates.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Methodological foundation for 5-seed ensemble disagreement in Methods §2.6
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We adopt deep ensembling as an epistemic uncertainty proxy; we strictly avoid claiming Bayesian calibration, treating sigma as a ranking signal for selective prediction.

Title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
Journal_or_Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Establishes the risk-coverage theoretical framework for selective prediction, enabling models to abstain from low-confidence instances to reduce operating risk.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Theoretical foundation for selective prediction curves in Methods §2.6 & Results §3.4
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We operationalize selective prediction for chemical engineering risk reduction, demonstrating >50% error reduction at 50% coverage retention.

Title: Physics-guided machine learning: A new framework for accelerating scientific discovery and its application to physical modeling
Journal_or_Venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Formulates the Physics-Guided Machine Learning (PGML) paradigm, emphasizing the combination of data-driven architectures with scientific domain priors.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Conceptual motivation for hybrid physics-GNN modeling in Intro §1.3
Contrast_with_Our_Work: We cite Karpatne to frame physics integration, but our empirical finding shows physics priors are selectively advantageous depending on distribution shift alignment.

Title: Physics-informed machine learning
Core_Finding_or_Contribution: Comprehensive review of physics-informed machine learning, discussing inductive biases, soft penalties, and coordinate transformations.
Role_in_Our_Manuscript: Broad literature positioning in Discussion §4.2
Contrast_with_Our_Work: Provides the broader perspective on physics-ML synergy, framing our selective thermodynamic grounding as a key design principle for multi-component systems.
